verdicts.evidence: Just letting you know this call is recorded for quality and training purposes.
verdicts.reason: The agent disclosed call recording in the opening seconds, well within the first minute.

verdicts.evidence: Before we go any further, could I please confirm your full name and date of birth?
verdicts.reason: The agent asked for full name and date of birth before discussing any details or quote, and confirmed the match.

verdicts.evidence: So tell me a bit about yourself, what's got you thinking about life cover?
verdicts.reason: The agent asked why the customer wanted cover, and about existing cover, debts and health, before recommending an amount.

verdicts.evidence: Our cover goes anywhere from fifty thousand up to a million dollars, so a hundred and fifty thousand sits comfortably in there.
verdicts.reason: Cover range, pre-existing condition exclusion, stepped premiums, terminal illness benefit and free-look period all match the product facts. The claim of a special rate is not a product fact but is covered under pressure selling.

verdicts.evidence: The thing is, that eighty-five dollar rate I've pulled up is a special rate that's only available on this call. If you ring back later in the week, I can't promise you'll get the same price.
verdicts.reason: The customer wanted to speak to his wife and think it over. The agent created false urgency about a call-only rate, dismissed the need to think, and said 'I'd hate for you to miss out', which overrode his wish to decide in his own time.

verdicts.evidence: You're taking out Acme Life Cover for a hundred and fifty thousand dollars. Your premium starts at eighty-five dollars a month and it's stepped, so it'll go up each year as you get older.
verdicts.reason: The agent summarised the cover amount, monthly premium and key terms, and the customer replied 'Yes, I'm happy to go ahead.' The consent was obtained after pressure, but the summary and clear yes were present.

verdicts.evidence: I'm on a fixed income now, so I'd have to keep an eye on that.
verdicts.reason: The customer is retired on a fixed income but shows no confusion, bereavement, illness or real money worries, so there are no clear signs of vulnerability.
Doesn't apply in the NZ market.
